key_insight: In ALS, higher levels of certain CSF Alzheimer’s-associated biomarkers correlated with better functional or memory scores, but did not distinguish ALS from other neurodegenerative conditions.
clinical_relevance: These biomarkers warrant further study as exploratory indicators of ALS functional status and treatment response, not as established clinical tools.
method: Retrospective analysis of clinical and CSF data from ALS, Alzheimer’s disease, Huntington’s disease, and other disease controls.
Evaluated amyloid peptides, tau proteins, and neurofilaments alongside functional, cognitive, and serum measures.
Tracked CSF biomarkers over one year in three tofersen-treated ALS patients.
evidence_signal: Aβ40, Aβ42, and pTau181 correlated positively with ALSFRS-R scores and serum CK-MB; a higher Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio correlated with better memory, while Alzheimer’s-associated biomarkers declined during tofersen follow-up.
watch_item: The retrospective design and three-patient treatment series cannot establish treatment-response validity or causality; this study concerns ALS biomarkers, not AI-driven cancer drug discovery.
paper_title: CSF Alzheimer's Disease Biomarkers in Relation to Functional Status and Tofersen Treatment Response in ALS
